title: Suzlon Q4 Results: Profit Dip, Revenue Up – What It Means
description: Suzlon Energy reported a 6% year-on-year dip in Q4 FY24 consolidated net profit to ₹281 crore, primarily due to exceptional items in the previous year. Despit.

faq.q: Why did Suzlon's Q4 profit dip despite revenue growth?
faq.a: Suzlon's Q4 FY24 net profit dipped by 6% year-on-year primarily because Q4 FY23 included certain exceptional items that boosted profits, creating a higher base for comparison. The underlying operational performance, as indicated by the 29% revenue growth, remained strong.

faq.q: What is the significance of Suzlon's debt reduction?
faq.a: Suzlon significantly reduced its consolidated net debt by 76% year-on-year to ₹310 crore. This is crucial as it strengthens the company's balance sheet, reduces interest expenses, improves financial stability, and enhances its ability to fund future growth organically.

faq.q: What does the 3.3 GW order book mean for Suzlon?
faq.a: A 3.3 GW (Gigawatt) order book represents a substantial pipeline of confirmed projects for Suzlon. It provides strong revenue visibility for the coming years, indicating future business and operational continuity, which is a positive sign for investors.

faq.q: Is Suzlon's performance indicative of the broader renewable energy sector in India?
faq.a: Suzlon's strong revenue growth and healthy order book reflect the positive momentum in India's renewable energy sector, driven by government targets and increasing demand for green energy. However, individual company performance can vary based on specific strategies, execution, and competitive landscape.

faq.q: How does EBITDA margin relate to a company's health?
faq.a: EBITDA margin (16.3% for Suzlon in Q4 FY24) indicates a company's operational profitability before accounting for non-operating expenses. A healthy EBITDA margin suggests efficient core business operations and cost management, which is a good sign for a company's financial health.

faq.q: What is the management's outlook for Suzlon?
faq.a: Management's outlook is positive, focusing on "profitable growth" and achieving a "debt-free status." They highlight a strong foundation built in FY24, a robust order book, and readiness to capitalise on India's renewable energy expansion.
